subject: Request: Temporary SLO tolerance & commercial waiver for Aurelia Therapeutics
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Aurelia - request: temporary SLO tolerance & commercial waiver

Team — quick summary and ask. Aurelia Therapeutics (pilot) is pushing to sign this week but procurement won’t accept the standard 99.95% uptime SLO for their multi-region inference workload. They are asking for a temporary tolerance of 99.90% for the first 3 months of the pilot and a corresponding cap on service credits. In exchange they want a one-time 20% onboarding discount and accelerated invoice terms.

Why this is urgent: their go/no-go is tied to a board demo scheduled 05/28; procurement says contract must be fully executed with revised SLO language and DocuSign by EOD Thursday.

What I’m proposing (deal desk recommendation):
- Temporal SLO tolerance: 99.90% uptime for pilot period (90 days) vs our standard 99.95%
- Cap on service credits: max credit exposure limited to $15k for the pilot period
- One-time onboarding discount: 20% off first three months of usage (applied to committed spend only)
- Operational requirements: Aurelia agrees to the standard remediation plan, daily incident reports when any threshold breach occurs, and a post-pilot review to revert to 99.95% or agree on long‑term terms

Attachments: I’ve attached Aurelia_SLO_Redline_20270522.pdf and a mutual action plan (RW-MAP-Aurelia-v3.xlsx).

Ask: Can I get exec clearance to sign the SLO tolerance + commercial waiver under the conditions above? If yes, please confirm exact phrasing we should accept and any additional guardrails from legal/product (Jonas, Lauren).

— Sofia
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurelia - request: temporary SLO tolerance & commercial waiver

Sofia — thanks for the clear ask. High level: I’m comfortable with a temporary tolerance for a pilot but want firm limits and escalation controls.

Items I need before I will sign off (executive clearance):
1) Legal to insert a one‑way credit cap and clear definition of "breach" window (rolling 30-day measurements).
2) Product to confirm there are no blockers to reversion to 99.95% after pilot and that we can enable additional autoscaling bursts for the pilot regionally.
3) Deal economics: confirm that the 20% onboarding discount is restricted to committed usage only and that the finance team signs invoice cadence (net-30 by default).

If the answers are affirmative, I can clear the tolerance and discount limited to the 90-day pilot and the $15k maximum remediation exposure. Jonas / Lauren — please advise on the contract language I should sign (exact sentence for SLO tolerance + cap).

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Aurelia - request: temporary SLO tolerance & commercial waiver

Jonas / Lauren — forwarding Sofia's note and the redline. Two quick asks for legal/product:

Jonas: can you add a short clause that explicitly limits credit liability to incidents that meet our measurable breach criteria and that credits are the sole remedy during the pilot (no termination or indemnity expansions)? Also suggest we require a weekly incident summary to be emailed to the CS/ops owners during the pilot.

Lauren: confirm product is okay with temporary 99.90% for 90 days and that we can configure autoscale allowances for the pilot region. If product wants additional telemetry hooks in the contract, flag that now.

The customer is sensitive on price; this 20% onboarding discount gets the board demo across the line. We should keep the discount timeboxed and tied to fully executed commitment.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurelia - request: temporary SLO tolerance & commercial waiver — redline + exec language

All — reviewed the attached redline and put the minimal protective language below. I’m ok with the pilot concession under the following cumulative conditions (if Marissa concurs we can scope into the contract):

Contract language (recommended):
"For the period commencing on the Effective Date and continuing for 90 days (the \"Pilot Period\"), Redwood agrees to a temporary Service Availability target of 99.90% for the Services defined herein. The parties agree that Service Credits are the exclusive remedy for any Service Availability shortfall during the Pilot Period, provided that (i) any single credit event is measured against a rolling 30-day measurement window, and (ii) Redwood's aggregate liability for Service Credits during the Pilot Period shall not exceed Fifteen Thousand United States Dollars (US $15,000)."

Additional guardrails and operational requirements:
- Customer must provide access to production traffic profiles and agree to a weekly incident digest to the Redwood operations owner.
- Any outage resulting from customer configuration (non-Redwood-managed network or client misconfiguration) is excluded from credit calculation.
- Post-pilot review: within 14 days of Pilot Period end the parties will meet to evaluate returning to standard SLO (99.95%) or negotiate long-term terms.

I also recommend we add the onboarding discount as an appendix referencing committed monthly spend and explicitly excluding usage beyond committed amounts from the discount. Finance to confirm the net‑30 cadence and that the discount is applied on invoice generation.

Marissa — if you approve this language I am comfortable with you executing the DocuSign envelope.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
